newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS' ACCUSER CHARGED BY POLICE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS' ACCUSER CHARGED BY POLICE.

text.p: A woman who falsely accused Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams of sexually assaulting her at gunpoint was herself charged on Tuesday with filing a false police report.
Police Sgt. Jim Chandler said Nina Shahravan, 23, was formally charged with the misdemeanor offence and would face up to six months in jail and a $2,000 fine if convicted.
Shahravan had accused Irvin of holding a gun against her head and threatening to kill her while Williams and a third man raped her on top of a pool table inside Williams' home on Dec. 29.
But she recanted her story last Friday after police confronted her with the evidence gathered during an 11-day investigation.
It was still not clear why Shahravan, a former topless dancer who has also worked at a mall makeup counter, made up the allegations against Williams and Irvin.
She was an acquaintance of Williams and had also known Irvin for some time. Chandler said Shahravan had 24 hours to turn herself in or pay a $500 bond, and that she would be arrested if she did not.

The allegations came days before the Cowboys, who have won three Super Bowls in the last four years, were eliminated from this year's title hunt in a second round playoff game against the Carolina Panthers.
Irvin, 30, and Williams, 28, are All-Pro stars who have played a key role in the Cowboys' success in the 1990s. Both players have been in trouble in the past.

Irvin is currently on four years probation after pleading no contest to felony cocaine possession charges last year. He was arrested after being found in a motel room with a former teammate and two strippers as well as drugs and sex toys.
If Irvin had been arrested on aggravated sexual assault charges, he could have had his probation revoked and been sent to jail.
Williams was in 1995 accused of sexually assaulting a 17-year-old topless dancer but a grand jury declined to indict him after he reached a settlement with the woman.
Both players insisted from the start that Shahravan's allegations were false and police said last Friday that the players had told the truth.

They players and their attorneys have sharply criticised the Dallas Police Department's handling of the case, and the way the media reported it. The attorneys have hinted at possible legal action against Shahravan, the police and some news organisations.
Shahravan's accusations sparked a wave of published attacks on the Cowboys team, which has been rocked by a string of drugs and sex scandals in the last two years.
